Evanescent

/ev-uh-NES-uhnt/ - the stress falls on NES · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Evanescent means lasting only a moment before vanishing.

An evanescent hush fell over the stadium between the kick and the roar, gone before anyone could name it.

Worked Example

The soap-bubble artist closes the children's show by filling the stage with a single bubble the size of a door. It trembles, throws rainbows across the front rows for four or five seconds, and is gone. No encore is possible — the next bubble is a different bubble — and the gasp in the dark is loudest at the exact instant there is nothing left to gasp at.

Evanescent is the precise word because the wonder is already dissolving as it appears; the audience is watching the disappearance itself. A short meeting is merely brief. Evanescent claims more: the thing fades before your eyes, and its going is part of what it is.

How Evanescent Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

vanishing

vanishing: already disappearing as you watch

short-lived

short-lived: lasting only a little while

Antonyms

enduring

enduring: lasting on and on, through wear and weather

permanent

permanent: fixed in place for good

How Strong Is It? — temporary → short-lived → evanescent

temporary vs. evanescent

temporary vs. evanescent: Temporary is the mildest rung — it promises only that a thing ends someday, maybe years out.

short-lived vs. evanescent

short-lived vs. evanescent: Short-lived stops short of evanescent: a short-lived fashion still gets its season, while an evanescent glow is dissolving in the very moment you notice it.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — e-

Prefix — e-: out, away

Root — van-

Root — van-: empty (Latin vanus)

Suffix — -escent

Suffix — -escent: becoming, in the process of

Put it together

Put it together: E- (away) + van- (empty) + -escent (becoming) = becoming empty away, emptying out even as you look. The -escent ending is the same "in the process of" found in adolescent; evanescent things are caught mid-vanish — the word describes a departure in progress, never a thing at rest.

Use the root in a new word: vanish

Use the root in a new word: vanish: The ferry seemed to vanish into the fog bank halfway across the strait.

Root Check

Word Choice

literary / poetic

Evanescent is for things caught dissolving — glows, hushes, scents, moods — and it carries a note of wistful admiration. Its neighbor in this unit, transient, is the cooler word: a transient guest still unpacks a bag and stays a while. Say transient for people, populations, and symptoms; save evanescent for what is fading even as you point at it.
